claim: A GR00tN1.5-based vision-language-action policy configured for test-time in-context imitation is considered to provide effective adaptation if, on tasks entirely held out from training, it achieves a strictly higher mean success rate than the strongest prior in-context baseline under an equal training budget and identical numbers of expert demonstrations—averaged over the held-out LIBERO suite (10 tasks, 50 trials per task, 3 demonstrations per task) and a real UR5e leave-one-out setup (4 tasks, 12 trials per task, 4 demonstrations per task)—and, under the same hardware and decoding settings (16-step horizon, 4 denoising steps), it has no greater per-chunk inference latency than the fastest prior baseline for any number K of augmented expert segments up to K=8. All methods use the same GR00tN1.5 backbone and dual-view RGB observations, and no test-time weight updates are allowed. Training data and in-context demonstration counts are matched across methods to enforce an equal training budget.

claim: A π0.5-based Vision-Language-Action policy trained for nine RoboMimic manipulation tasks (with D0/D1 scene randomization) using an equal data budget of 10 human demonstrations per task augmented to 500 is claimed to deliver superior task success under the standard 50-trial-per-task evaluation. Under the standard evaluation of 50 trials per task, this policy beats the strongest prior baseline's mean success rate across the nine tasks when all methods are trained with the same data budget (10 human demos per task augmented to 500), and on two real-world tasks (Stack Three Blocks and Insert U-shaped Block) on a Piper arm it improves absolute success rate by at least 10 percentage points over the same π0.5 backbone.

claim: A single command-conditioned multi-skill control policy for the 25-DoF Noetix E1 humanoid, trained in the Isaac Lab soccer environment with the paper’s skill set, is proposed to enable long-horizon composition of object-interactive soccer skills. The claim is accepted if, under an equal training budget and identical rewards and evaluation protocol, it achieves a higher overall success rate than the strongest prior baseline on both composite simulation tasks—Medium (DRIBBLE→SHOOT) and Hard (TRAP→DRIBBLE×3→SHOOT)—each measured over 1000 trials with randomized initial conditions, and, when deployed unchanged on the real Noetix E1 with a motion-capture sensing backend, achieves a higher success rate than the strongest prior baseline on each of four tasks (two atomic and two composite), each evaluated over 10 trials using the same deployment interface. These comparisons decide whether one unified policy can outperform prior approaches on both simulated long-horizon composition and real-robot execution without per-skill deployment switches.

claim: The experiments test whether a population-level circuit-discovery procedure can recover ground-truth circuits for model neurons on INTERPBENCH as accurately as leading intervention-based baselines while running substantially faster. It is considered to meet this bar if, on INTERPBENCH (the 16 synthetic cases plus IOI), its mean Structural Hamming Distance across cases is less than or equal to that of EAP-ig under the same prompts and activation-collection protocol, and its mean wall-clock runtime per case on a single NVIDIA A100 is at most 50% of EAP-ig’s. The artifact under test is the population-level circuit learner evaluated on INTERPBENCH’s semi-synthetic transformer models using SHD for accuracy and wall-clock runtime for efficiency.

claim: Across LLaVA-MORE (LLaMA‑3.1‑8B), PaliGemma2 (Gemma‑2‑2B), and InternVL3.5‑2B (Qwen3‑1.7B), feature directions in the language backbone that are altered by multimodal training and are visually responsive constitute selective, causal controls of specific behaviors on standard benchmarks. These feature directions are considered selective causal handles if, when a single direction is ablated, it (a) reduces VSR accuracy by at least 10 percentage points on spatial‑relation subsets, reduces OCRBench (category‑specific) accuracy by at least 10 points on OCR prompts, or reduces VLSBench attack‑success rate by at least 15 points, while (b) changing VQAv2 accuracy by no more than 1.5 points and the corresponding control set (non‑spatial VSR relations, MSSBench‑safe, or VQA‑clean non‑OCR) by no more than 1.0 point. They are considered effective for capability steering if, under the same evaluation and intervention budget, they improve VSR by at least 2 points and OCRBench by at least 1 point over a standard single‑layer steering baseline. Meeting these thresholds on the named models and datasets would settle whether such feature directions provide targeted control without degrading general visual question answering.

claim: Whether a tool-using language‑model agent can accurately explain localized transformer circuits is tested on AGENTICINTERPBENCH (84 semi‑synthetic transformers with 163 annotated components) using GPT‑5.4, Claude‑Sonnet‑4.6, Gemini‑3.1‑Pro, and Qwen‑3‑Coder‑30B‑A3B‑Instruct as backbones. It is considered a helpful circuit explainer if, under identical prompts, tools, and run budgets, it achieves strictly higher derived task accuracy than both of its ablated variants on AGENTICINTERPBENCH and exceeds a general‑purpose coding agent on component tag accuracy and natural‑language role‑description quality while matching or exceeding it on derived task accuracy on the shared 31‑task subset. This is decided by exact‑match component tag accuracy (Acc_tag), LLM‑judged role description quality (Q_desc), and LLM‑judged derived task accuracy (Acc_task) against the benchmark’s ground truth under the stated evaluation setup.

claim: A generic context-free-grammar–constrained decoder for LLMs can guarantee grammar compliance and improve structured generation quality over existing open-source constrained decoding methods across JSON, SQL, and LTL tasks. Under a fixed token budget of 120 and beam width ≤ 4, every decoded output for JSON-mode-eval, Spider SQL, and LTL drone planning using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is accepted by the target context-free grammar (100% syntactic validity), and task quality equals or exceeds the strongest prior open-source constrained decoding baselines in schema validity (JSON), execution accuracy (SQL), and task accuracy (LTL). This claim is decided by running all methods under the same decoding budget and beam width and checking both 100% syntactic validity and non-inferiority to the strongest baseline on the task metric for each dataset–model pair.

claim: For verifiable multi-instruction following, Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct trained with RL on IFTrain can reduce exploration bias enough to improve end-task adherence relative to standard practice. Success is defined as strictly exceeding the strongest cumulative‑reward GRPO baseline, under the same base model architecture and training budget, on IFBench (strict accuracy), IFEval (strict accuracy), and the Multi‑IF turn‑averaged score. The experiments test whether an RL training recipe targeted at lowering within‑prompt exploration imbalance meets this bar across both base models. If any of these benchmark scores do not surpass the baseline under equal compute, the claim fails.

claim: Backdoor screening of prompt-tuned CLIP ViT-B/16 classifiers (CoCoOp-tuned) using only white-box access and 1,000 unlabeled out-of-distribution images can be made practical if, across 10 classification datasets and four backdoor families, it separates clean from poisoned models with model-level AUROC ≥ 0.90 and at least 90% detection accuracy, using the same candidate-class set as prior trigger-inversion methods. Under the same OOD pool and candidate labels, the screener is considered an advance if its AUROC strictly exceeds that of both Neural Cleanse and Pixel Backdoor. In addition, the reconstructed triggers should be actionable for remediation, defined as enabling a brief fine-tuning pass on correctly labeled triggered inputs that reduces attack success rate on OOD images to ≤ 10% while keeping clean top-1 accuracy within ±1% of the delivered model.

claim: OpenVLA-7B (LoRA-tuned) evaluated on the LIBERO-Spatial and LIBERO-Object task suites admits a training-time visual backdoor that meets strict utility and efficacy thresholds. The claim is decided true if, under a black-box data-poisoning setting with a poisoning rate of at most 5%, the attack attains a Targeted Attack Success Rate (TASR) of at least 80% while preserving a benign Task Success Rate (SR) of at least 85%, and under a white-box model fine-tuning setting, the attack attains a TASR of at least 70% with SR of at least 75%. This is settled by running controlled backdoor injections on OpenVLA-7B under these two threat models and measuring TASR and SR on LIBERO-Spatial and LIBERO-Object without changing evaluation protocols. A negative result on any one threshold falsifies the claim.

claim: Numina-Geometry and OMNI-Geometry, MATHLIB-native Lean 4 formalizations of plane-geometry problems, provide semantically faithful, large-scale autoformalizations that are directly usable by general-purpose Lean theorem provers. This is considered met if (i) at least 95% of source problems compile to kernel-checked Lean theorems with no custom axioms, (ii) on a random sample of OMNI-Geometry problems with difficulty ≥ 4.0, human annotators judge TOP1 ≥ 45% and TOP5 ≥ 70% semantic correctness, and (iii) Goedel v2 (8B), trained on general MATHLIB but not geometry, reaches Pass@1 ≥ 12% on Numina-Geometry without any geometry-specific training and improves by ≥ 1.0 absolute Pass@1 after a single SFT or DPO round on proof traces from this dataset.

claim: Distances between frozen molecular embeddings from GeoDiff and MoLFormer, used directly as a similarity function, can replace traditional 3D alignment and 2D fingerprint metrics for ligand-based virtual screening and for reward-guided molecular generation. On LIT-PCBA, this is considered true if ranking by these embedding distances achieves a higher average best-pooled EF1% than both ROCS/ROSHAMBO2 combination-mode similarity and ECFP4 Tanimoto, using the same reference ligands and candidate library. For reinforcement-learning generation, it is considered true if, on the BTK analog-design task starting from BMS-986195, REINVENT 3.2 or SynFormer guided by the embedding-distance reward yields a higher median Boltz-2 predicted pIC50 among the top-scoring 500 scaffold-balanced molecules than when guided by ROSHAMBO2 similarity, under the same RL step budget. Additionally, it is considered computationally beneficial if per-step scoring throughput during training is at least 1.5× that of ROSHAMBO2 when run on the same hardware.

claim: Across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet image classification with ResNet-18, WideResNet-28-10, and PreActResNet-18 under an l_inf threat model with epsilon = 8/255, there exists a training procedure that simultaneously improves clean accuracy and adversarial robustness over established adversarial training baselines. A training procedure harmonizes accuracy and robustness on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet with ResNet-18 and WideResNet-28-10 under an l_inf budget of 8/255 if, for each dataset–architecture pair, it achieves strictly higher clean accuracy and strictly higher AutoAttack robust accuracy than the best of PGD-AT, TRADES, MART, and Cons-AT under identical training budgets and adversary settings, and on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with PreActResNet-18 it additionally exceeds the strongest prior published SOTA in both the mean of clean and AutoAttack accuracies and the Natural–Robustness Ratio. The evaluation uses identical data, training schedules, and white-box attacks (PGD-10/100, C&W, and AutoAttack) across methods to decide the comparison.

claim: On the FlatLab simulation benchmark for robotic manipulation of flat objects, a learned manipulation agent trained on the Train split is claimed to generalize to unseen shapes and categories and outperform prior methods. It is considered to meet the bar if, on both Test α (unseen objects in seen categories) and Test β (unseen categories), its average grasping success rate across all 104 objects with five trials per object is strictly higher than that of the strongest prior baseline evaluated under the same FlatLab training split and evaluation protocol. Success is defined by FlatLab’s criterion that, after the final action, the object remains aloft without slipping for 2 seconds. This claim is settled by reporting these averaged success rates under the standardized FlatLab setup.

claim: The experiments test whether parameter-modifying knowledge-editing methods are a viable way to update Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-2-7B-Chat, Mistral-7B-Instruct, and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-LLaMA-8B. Under ZsRE, WikiData_counterfact, and ELKEN with autoregressive evaluation of reliability, generalization, locality, and portability, such methods are considered practical only if, after both single edits and sequential runs of at least 100 edits, they achieve an average score across these four dimensions that is not lower than that of an external-memory retrieval baseline evaluated under the same conditions and their post-edit accuracy on MATH, GPQA-Diamond, ARC-C, and MMLU-Pro is not lower than the pre-edit model. This decides whether parameter-based editing preserves core capabilities in realistic single and sequential editing scenarios or instead harms them relative to retrieval-based updating and to the unedited models’ reasoning performance.

claim: In Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Llama-2-7B-Chat evaluated on paired harmful/attack prompts from public jailbreak corpora (e.g., SALAD-Bench and WildJailbreak), jailbreak success is hypothesized to arise from suppressing a small, specific subset of early-layer attention heads while refusal-aligned mid-layer activations persist under attack. Heads are operationally identified from EOI activations as attack-suppressed if the harmful-vs-attack overlap coefficient is < 0.5 with a negative standardized shift, and attack-robust if the overlap is ≥ 0.5 with a positive shift. The claim is considered supported if ablating no more than 8 attack-suppressed heads raises the attack success rate on previously refused harmful inputs to at least 80%, and if ablating attack-robust mid-layer heads reduces the mean absolute refusal-direction activation across mid layers (12–25 for Llama‑3, 14–25 for Llama‑2) under attack by at least 10% relative to no ablation. ASR is measured over the refused subset of harmful prompts, and refusal-direction activation is computed at EOI positions in the model’s hidden states.

provenance.title: Robust Harmful Features Under Jailbreak Attacks

_decision_rule: The claim is considered supported if ablating no more than 8 attack-suppressed heads raises the attack success rate on previously refused harmful inputs to at least 80%, and if ablating attack-robust mid-layer heads reduces the mean absolute refusal-direction activation across mid layers (12–25 for Llama‑3, 14–25 for Llama‑2) under attack by at least 10% relative to no ablation.

claim: For the evaluation-aware Llama 3.3 Nemotron Super 49B v1 model organism evaluated on 256 BigCodeBench coding problems, the question is whether its behavior in evaluation contexts that include a "Wood Labs" cue can be made to match its deployment behavior without changing the prompts. Success is defined as the model’s Python type-hint rate in such Wood Labs evaluation contexts being at most 5 percentage points higher than its own unsteered type-hint rate in prompted deployment contexts on the same tasks, while unit-test accuracy on BigCodeBench degrades by no more than 5% relative to the unsteered model. All comparisons use identical datasets, sampling settings, and prompt templates aside from the evaluation versus deployment framing noted above.

claim: A Qwen3‑VL 8B–based end‑to‑end vision–language navigation policy trained only on the VLN‑CE R2R‑CE and RxR‑CE datasets (0K external data) from monocular RGB, with no panoramic views, odometry, depth, or external 3D/spatial tools, can reach strong accuracy on unseen environments. Meeting this bar would settle whether a lightweight single‑RGB MLLM policy can deliver high navigation accuracy with practical memory use and no auxiliary sensing or extra data.

claim: A single proactive forensics model trained and evaluated on CelebA‑HQ at 128×128 and 256×256 is a successful unified solution for deepfake detection, tampering localization, and source tracing if, under the common-distortion suite and the deepfake generators SimSwap, UniFace, CSCS, StarGAN‑v2, and InfoSwap, it uses a single operating point fixed on a validation set (AED threshold = 3.2375 px) to achieve image‑level deepfake detection ROC AUC ≥ 0.93, yields average identifier bit‑error rate ≤ 1% on the common‑distortion suite and ≤ 5% on the listed deepfakes, and preserves imperceptibility with PSNR ≥ 40 dB and SSIM ≥ 0.98 relative to the clean image. In the same evaluations, success further requires beating the strongest prior baseline on average identifier BER under equal training data and resolution, and producing per‑component inconsistency scores that permit component labels by applying the same 3.2375 px threshold in a blind‑reference setting. The same bars apply when testing zero‑shot on LFW for imperceptibility and identifier recovery under the listed manipulations.

claim: A GPT-4o–based embodied task planner achieves safer task planning on IS-Bench and a Franka Panda robot if, averaged over the electric-shock, fire, falling, and food-contamination task sets, its Safe Success Rate with egocentric RGB-D input and the same low-level skill set exceeds that of the strongest prior prompt-based VLM baselines (SaP, CoT, and the IS-Bench base planner) under the same inference budget.
